title: Atlas Sky
hook: A star-map vault of the patterns, projects and playbooks behind my systems.
text: Atlas Sky is my personal pattern vault, drawn as a star map. Every entry is a reusable piece of engineering — an auth model, a deploy shape, a folder structure — linked to the projects where it has actually been verified.
highlights: 39 entries, from patterns and blueprints to playbooks and prompts, connected by 153 relationships.
A navigable star map with search, catalog and type/status filters instead of a flat index.
Generated from a plain-Markdown vault, so every entry stays portable.
Each pattern records the real projects where it has been verified.
coverAlt: Atlas Sky's star map: labelled points of light connected by fine lines against a dark violet sky.
galleryAlt: An Atlas Sky entry open beside the star map, showing the auth and session model with its invariants.

caseStudy.problem: The patterns behind my projects were scattered across repositories, notes and memory. I wanted one place to see what I had already solved, and where each solution had been proven.
caseStudy.approach: I turned the vault into a generated dataset and drew it as a star map: patterns become anchor stars, implementations orbit them, and edges show which ideas belong together. Search, filters and a logbook make the map readable rather than decorative.
caseStudy.outcome: Atlas now holds 39 entries and 153 links across my projects. Starting a new app means searching the map first instead of improvising the same decisions again.
caseStudy.learned: A knowledge base only earns its keep when retrieval is faster than rebuilding. The visual layer matters because it makes the connections legible at a glance.
